The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 29.59% to 29.04%. Restated at replacement capex: NVO spent 133,110mm DKK on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 19,625mm DKK of plant depreciation, 13.64% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 29.04% to 11.89%. Restated with selling costs: SG&A now carries NVO's filed selling or distribution costs, 20.81% of revenue this charge was absorbing, so it falls from 11.89% to nil. The filed lines alone now leave less than the cash the company made before interest and at replacement capex, and a charge below nil would credit the book with cash its own costs do not leave. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 41.40% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 50.32%, so the charge rebuilds at -8.92%. It was held at nil, but NVO books 6,529mm DKK of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0000353278-26-000012), 2.11% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -2.11%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVO's cash flow statement shows receivables up 20,296mm DKK, inventories up 25,235mm DKK, payables up 15,158mm DKK, a working capital build of 30,373mm DKK, 3.65% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -2.11% where the filed figures rebuild it at -8.92%, and stays there.
